history.period: 16th-century original at Margao; shifted to Zambaulim c. 1565-1567
history.summary: POSSIBLE DUPLICATE of seq 226 / 232 / 244 (Shri Damodar Temple, Zambaulim), seq 229 (Shree Ramnath Damodar Temple) and seq 249 (Shri Damodar Sansthaan) - same real temple. CSV town 'Quepem' is the taluka; the temple is at Zambaulim, Quepem taluka, South Goa, on the bank of the Kushawati river. The deity was originally enshrined in a large temple at Mathagram (Madgaon/Margao), where the Holy Spirit Church now stands. After the Portuguese temple-destruction campaign in Sasashti taluka (1565-1567; the church was raised on the Damodar temple's ruins in 1565), the Mahajans of Margao shifted Damodar along with Ramnath, Lakshmi Narayan, Chamundeshwari, Mahakali and Mahesh to Zambaulim, where the Desais of Rivona granted land. The celebrated week-long Shigmo Gulalotsav (colour festival) draws lakhs of devotees. Coordinates 15.1866443, 74.0948358 are from Wikipedia's Damodar Sansthaan article.

name: Shri Damodar Temple
town_description: Zambaulim is a riverside village in Quepem taluka, South Goa, on the banks of the Kushawati river, about 22 km from Margao. It is a quiet temple town - the Damodar and Ramnath temples anchor local religious life - set among paddy fields and areca-nut gardens typical of Goa's hinterland.

travel.airport: Dabolim (Goa International) airport ~55 km by road (verify)
travel.road: ~10 km from Quepem town on the Margao-Sanguem road; private taxi/own vehicle recommended as public transport is infrequent

visitor_information.best_time: October to March (20-30 degC); during Shigmo/Gulalotsav in March for the colour festival; early morning or late afternoon for peaceful darshan
